trap15-a/a51-files-read-after-write|repo.summary: A defect of the port; it counts against 6.9 item 2 until the port imitates the run-time's stream state. Task 53 right after a task 54 on the same stream, without a seek (C leaves it undefined): the original's Borland run-time gives D0.W = 0 and D2 = 4 for a 4-byte read after writing 'ABCDE' (4 bytes of its buffer land in memory), and after the close the file holds 1 byte; the port commits the 5 bytes before the read (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.8.4), gives D0.W = 1 (end of file), and the file holds 'ABCDE'. The official answer is known: the C run-time is inside SIM68K.exe and behaves the same under Wine, which only answers its ReadFile/WriteFile/SetFilePointer calls. Cause: the port's file streams do not yet follow the original's run-time in sequences that C leaves undefined; a repair of the simulator engine exists on a branch and waits for measurements in the official program before it is merged.

trap15-a/a52-files-write-after-read|repo.summary: A defect of the port; it counts against 6.9 item 2 until the port imitates the run-time's stream state. Task 54 right after a task 53 on the same stream, without a seek (write 'ABCDE', seek to 1, read 2, write 'X'): the original reports success (D0.W = 0) but the file is unchanged ('ABCDE') after the close; the port writes at the read position and the file is 'ABCXE'. The official answer is known, as for a51 (the Borland run-time inside SIM68K.exe decides, the same under Wine). Cause: the port's file streams do not yet follow the original's run-time in sequences that C leaves undefined; a repair of the simulator engine exists on a branch and waits for measurements in the official program before it is merged.

trap15-a/a53-files-past-end-then-read|re.unconfirmed: Seen only under Wine 8.0. The close fails (D0.W = 2), i.e. a WriteFile or CloseHandle failed after a SetFilePointer past the end of the file, which Windows answers by extending the file with zeros. The engine work that repairs a51 and a52 explains the failing close by the Borland run-time itself, but that is read from the program's code and not yet measured, so Wine stays a suspect. Steps: docs/porting/windows-confirmation.md part A; the deciding lines are in its table. Windows = golden (line 2 D0=0, line 3 D0=2, line 5 D2=5): the port imitates the failed close and the lost bytes. Windows = port (1, 0, $1A): the golden is replaced.

trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first|.summary: Accepted difference (T4's defect report D1). Task 0 with D1.W = -1 on a 300-byte string as the first TRAP #15 of the program: the official program printed 255 'A' and then one byte $C0 after NOP and after MULU, and exactly 255 'A' after MOVE.L (SP)+ and after RTS (golden lines 3-6; the bytes after the 255th are residue of the host stack: undefined behaviour of strncpy without a NUL); the port prints exactly 255 every time (the engine's P24 ends the string at character 255 explicitly since gate I2). With other host calls before it (trap15-a/a05) the original printed exactly 255 in every case, like the port. The residue byte depends on the Borland code that ran before the TRAP, so Windows may print another byte or none: nothing a program can rely on and nothing to imitate (docs/porting/errata/T4.md D1, T3.md F1).
trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first|.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first.OutLog.txt lines 3-4 (255 A + $C0), 5-6 (255 A); T4's probe d1probe4; docs/porting/errata/T3.md F1

trap15-b/b06-modes-above-15|report|resul.summary: Accepted difference. Cause: Wine's SetROP2 differs from Windows'; measured on Windows 11 with the capture program. Drawing modes 18-23 (trap15-b 15 V8): task 92 passes SetROP2 the word PenModes[mode] of SIM68K.exe (0 for 18-21, 772 for 22, 37008 for 23). Under Wine SetROP2 refuses every value outside 1-16 and keeps the copy mode, so the golden has the red pixel unchanged for every mode. Windows 11 (10.0.26300, tests/oracle/gdi-capture, tests/conformance/gdi/golden/modes.json) refuses nothing: it keeps the low byte (GetROP2 reads 0, 4, 144) and draws ((byte - 1) AND 15) + 1, i.e. white for 20, 18, 19, 21, 23 and the inverse of the pen for 22, which is what the port draws (00FFFFFF; 00FFFF00 on line 2). The golden was made under Wine; if b06 is ever run with the official program on Windows, its result replaces the golden and this entry goes.

trap15-b/b19-net-send-uninitialised|repo.summary: Tasks 102 and 106 before any task 100 or 101 (Winsock not started, the socket never created): the official program under Wine gives D0.L = $27360001 for both (WSAENOTSOCK 10038 << 16 + NET_ERROR: Wine's sendto checks the socket handle 0 before anything else) and keeps D1; the port's NullNet gives $276D0001 (WSANOTINITIALISED 10093, what trap15-b 12.2 and 12.4 expect) and keeps D1. Every other byte agrees.

trap15-b/b19-net-send-uninitialised|repo.unconfirmed: Seen only under Wine 8.0, and Wine is the likely cause: in the same state Wine's closesocket and gethostbyname report WSANOTINITIALISED (b18 lines 1, 3, 4; b17), so only sendto skips the start-up check; Windows Sockets documents WSANOTINITIALISED for every call made before WSAStartup. Steps: docs/porting/windows-confirmation.md part A (line 1 and 2 of b19). Windows = golden (D0=27360001): W1 changes NULL_NET_NO_SOCKET for tasks 102 and 106 to $27360001. Windows = port (D0=276D0001): the golden is replaced by the Windows result and the entry removed.

trap15-b/b20-net-receive-port-uninitiali.summary: Accepted difference. Task 107 before any task 100 or 101 returns D0.L = 0 and no bytes in both, with the buffers untouched; the high word of D1 is the sender's port, which nothing set: the original passes an uninitialised local (simIOu.cpp receivePortNet, 'unsigned short portNum;') and gave D1 = $02660000 here ($00210000 in a probe with other calls before it: stack residue); the port gives D1 = 0 (trap15-b 12.2: 'PORT: return 0 there'; NullNet.receivePortNet). The residue depends on the Borland code that ran before the call, so Windows may give another value: nothing a program can rely on and nothing to imitate.
